Gannon states Celtic boss Martin O’Neill boss ran out of his post-match media conference to tie up Gineitis deal…

Six in, four loans, one fee undisclosed, and £3.5 million the biggest outlay. Just another typical end to a typical Celtic transfer window, and almost £20 million in profit made.

Eric Knott 3rd September 2026 5 minutes read

Last night, Michael Gannon of the Record said that Celtic boss Martin O’Neill had cut his post-match media conference short to rush out the door and get more signings in.

Aberdeen boss Stephen Robinson says his side are looking forward to the visit of Derek McInnes' Rangers on Sunday, and are targeting victory against the struggling Ibrox outfit.

"Don't think it's a penalty" | Rangers' Derek McInnes on Hibs loss

The strange thing about Gannon’s piece was that he said O’Neill was trying to finalise both the Jordan Lotomba and Gvidas Gineitis deals.

He said this when confirmation was already through that the Gineitis deal had collapsed.

Why would Gannon say that?

Needless to say, today is deadline day, and Gineitis is not a Celtic player.

Unless Martin O’Neill can perform miracles, he won’t be either.

So why did Michael Gannon state this?

Was the deal dead or not at that point?

Well, if it wasn’t then, it certainly is now because even if Celtic did manage to sign Gineitis today, it’s too late.

He’s ineligible to play in the Europa League.

So, I’m pretty sure we can forget that one.

Just for posterity, here’s what Gannon had to say:

Martin O’Neill RACED out of his Aberdeen post-match press conference in a bid to complete MORE transfer deals on a wild European deadline day.

The Celtic boss landed Chelsea duo Shim Mhueka and Landon Emenalo and keeper Sam Johnstone all on loan for the season plus midfield prospect Joel van den Berg on a £3.4m move from PSV.

But O’Neill legged it out of his press briefing as he faced a race against the clock to complete deals for Torino midfielder Gvidas Gineitas and Feyenoord full back Jordan Lotomba.

Jordan Lotomba, on the other hand, is confirmed, with the 28 year old signing on for a one year deal.

No fee has been mentioned as yet.

I can only assume that this was a mistake on Gannon’s behalf, and that he didn’t mean to include Gvidas Gineitis in his reporting?

Martin O’Neill spoke like he was delighted with the business conducted by Celtic in the last couple of days.

Which is contrary to the reports that he was pretty angry over the failure to secure Gvidas Gineitis.

While we got the late night announcement on the Celtic website about Jordan Lotomba and Joel van den Berg, there was nothing about Gineitis.

So, on that basis, you can assume that the deal is well and truly dead in the water.

In reality, this was a typical end to a typical Celtic transfer window.

With only £3.4 million pounds actually spent in the closing stages of the window, and around £10 million raked in on the sales of Reo Hatate and Johnny Kenny, there must be an awful lot of self-congratulating going on in the Celtic boardroom.

They have managed to turn close to a £20 million profit in this transfer window.

In addition, and at the end of it all, 21 players have left the club.

That includes the conclusion of loan deals as well as players we have loaned out ourselves.

How successful this window turns out to be?

Only time will tell us that.

But the collapse of the Gineitis deal, along with the farcical messing around with Crystal Palace and Justin Devenny, typifies the behaviour of the board.

In the end, like a casino, the house always wins.

The Celtic board have once again proven that they will never exit a transfer window in a deficit.

Because if that happened, it would signal the end, wouldn’t it?

Celtic would go the same way as the dead club over the Ibrox way.

We would be headed for bankruptcy and liquidation.

So kudos to the Celtic board for once again saving our club from an ignominious end.

It’s always about the money at Celtic.

Where every pound is a prisoner, and profit is the Prince.

Aren’t we just blessed?

We’ll never die under these guys.

Amazing.

Key Takeaways

  • Michael Gannon reported that Martin O’Neill rushed to secure two signings, but Gineitis’s deal had already collapsed.
  • Deadline day confirms that Gineitis will not join Celtic, and any late signing is too late for the Europa League.
  • Jordan Lotomba has officially signed a one-year deal with Celtic, though no fee was disclosed.
  • O’Neill appeared pleased with recent transfers, despite frustration over missing out on Gineitis.
  • Celtic profited nearly £20 million this transfer window, spending only £3.4 million while selling players like Hatate and Kenny.
